title: Riesz-transform Schrodinger equation
plain: Couple a 2D Schrodinger wave to the Riesz transform of its own density. Mass is conserved, but there is no energy. Do smooth solutions live forever? R_1 is real and antisymmetric, so the potential is real, mass is conserved, there is no conserved energy, and the momentum P_1 = Im ∫ ū ∂_1 u is monotone. Data with small L^2 norm are global by Strichartz estimates; the question concerns large data.
math: Consider $iu_t+\Delta u=u\,R_1(|u|^2)$ on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^2$, $\widehat{R_1f}(\xi)=-i\frac{\xi_1}{|\xi|}\hat f(\xi)$. $R_1$ is real and antisymmetric, so mass is conserved and there is no conserved energy; small-mass data are global by Strichartz. Decide whether every Schwartz datum $u_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ gives a global solution $u\in C(\mathbb R,\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2))$ (classical, $u(0)=u_0$), or some datum blows up in finite time.
review_note: L^2-critical, non-Hamiltonian model: small mass is global, large data open.
refs: J.-M. Ghidaglia and J.-C. Saut, On the initial value problem for the Davey-Stewartson systems, Nonlinearity 3 (1990) (closest Hamiltonian analogue)
